text:
Hiring memo - Staff Motion Planning Engineer (req 2291)

Candidate: T. Wierzba
Current employer: Tessaro Robotics (Senior Motion Planning Engineer, 6 years)
Proposed level: IC6

Summary
Tomasz went through the full loop on Tuesday: coding, system design, a robotics deep dive and the HM conversation. Three of four interviewers are strong hire, one is lean hire. The concern from the coding round was speed; the deep dive more than made up for it. He walked us through how he approaches contact-rich grasp planning without sharing anything confidential, which the panel appreciated.

Level discussion
The HM originally proposed IC5. Given his scope at Tessaro (he informally leads four engineers and owns the planner roadmap), the panel agreed IC6 is the right call. Calibration with the Controls org is on Friday.

Compensation
He is currently at roughly $196k base with an RSU grant that vests in May. To make him whole we propose $214k base, 14,000 RSUs over four years and a $55k sign-on, split across two payments. Tomasz has said he won't entertain a counter from Tessaro if we land above $210k.

Risks
- Non-compete: he is based in California, so we don't expect enforcement, but legal will review his current contract.
- Timing: he wants to start after the May vest.

Recommendation: extend an offer this week.
note: Long memo; 'Tessaro' listed once to cover both 'Tessaro Robotics' and later short mentions.

Weekly talent market digest

1. Industry news. Hyundai keeps investing in Boston Dynamics, and ABB opened a new robotics campus in Shanghai a few years ago that is still hiring aggressively. Tessaro Robotics announced a new assembly plant in Ohio this week according to local press; no hiring numbers were published. Amazon continues to talk publicly about its Sparrow and Proteus robots.

2. Market pay. Public pay-transparency postings in Massachusetts show senior robotics software ranges clustering around $150,000 to $200,000. Several companies now advertise a competitive salary without any figure, which candidates increasingly dislike.

3. Process trends. More teams are moving to structured scorecards with a strong hire / hire / no hire scale, and asynchronous hiring memos instead of live debriefs for senior roles. Candidates tell us that a clear level framework (Engineer I through Principal) makes offers easier to compare.

4. Reading list. Laszlo Bock's Work Rules! and Reid Hoffman's The Alliance keep coming up in manager training. A good reminder that placeholders like [Candidate Name] in templates should always be replaced before sending.
